assumptions: Quality scores are Phred at the stated offset; FastQC does not infer it.
The adapter list is the one the library could carry (FastQC's own list unless one is given).
limits: No k-mer module: FastQC's own defaults switch it off.
bio.jane/contract.noReading: FastQC's own answer is a pass, warn or fail grade per module, which the outputs carry; the FASTQ canvas draws those grades and writes no sentence over them.
bio.jane/contract.question: Is this FASTQ run fit to use, module by module, the way a FastQC report would grade it?

description: FastQC's report on FASTQ reads, every module a default FastQC run reports: per-base quality boxes, per-tile quality (when the headers carry a tile), per-sequence quality, per-base sequence content, per-sequence GC against FastQC's theoretical normal, per-base N content, sequence length distribution, duplication levels, overrepresented sequences with their possible source, and adapter content, each with FastQC's own pass/warn/fail grade and the limit it was graded on. The numbers are FastQC 0.13.0's, checked against the real program, including its quirks: a read's mean quality is the integer mean of its characters, GC is counted on the read cut to a whole 100 (or 1,000) bases, duplication is counted on the first 50 bases, and an adapter found at a position counts at every position after it, so the curve is cumulative. FastQC does not detect the encoding: Phred+33 unless you say 64. It does not trim or filter anything.

_files.description: The project: record references shaped like _subject. Their records become library documents a tool names in sequences/parts/document; a trace or alignment is found by file name.

_subject.description: The record to act on: exactly one of sequence, accession (+source), sample (an id from list_samples) or file ({name, text} or {name, base64}); record_index picks one record of several.

adapters.description: adapters to search for, in FastQC's --adapters format (a name, a tab, a sequence, one per line). Unset searches FastQC's own list. Advanced.

contaminants.description: sequences an overrepresented read is matched against for its possible source, in FastQC's --contaminants format (a name, a tab, a sequence, one per line). Unset uses FastQC's own list. Advanced.

grouping.description: how read positions pool into one group: FastQC's default (the first 9 bases one by one, then groups sized to stay under 75), none (one per base, --nogroup) or exponential (--expgroup).

phred_offset.description: quality encoding: 33 for every modern FASTQ, 64 only for pre-1.8 Illumina (FastQC's --phred64). Advanced.

reads.description: the reads, as FASTQ: four lines per record, quality line required.

name: fastq_qc

failed.description: how many modules FastQC would fail

gcDeviationPercent.description: how far the per-read GC distribution sits from FastQC's normal, as a percent of reads

grades.description: module name to pass, warn or fail

report.description: every module's table and grade: perBaseQuality (boxes), perTileQuality (null without tiles), perSequenceQuality, perBaseContent, perSequenceGc (counts, theoretical, mode, stdev, deviationPercent), nContent, lengthDistribution, duplication (percentOfTotal, percentRemaining), overrepresented (sequences with count, percentage, possibleSource), adapterContent
